official_measurement_examples.name: Responsible-body currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: The designated responsible body list was updated 14 May 2026; only the Secretary of State or a designated responsible body can enter the statutory conservation-covenant regime with a landowner.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local land charge status
official_measurement_examples.fact: A conservation covenant is a local land charge and the responsible body must arrange registration on the appropriate Local Land Charges register.

official_measurement_examples.name: Voluntary but binding
official_measurement_examples.fact: The agreement is voluntary when created, but qualifying obligations become legally binding and can bind future landowners; this is not the same as planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public access separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Public access is not required for a conservation covenant and must not be inferred from covenant existence.

official_measurement_examples.name: BNG legal agreement role
official_measurement_examples.fact: A conservation covenant can be one legal mechanism securing a biodiversity gain site for at least 30 years, but covenant existence alone does not prove gain-site registration or unit allocation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ownership evidence separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A covenant requires a qualifying land interest, but a covenant or LLC search result is not a substitute for current title-register verification.

official_measurement_examples.name: Pre-existing designations
official_measurement_examples.fact: A conservation covenant can relate to land with or without an existing statutory designation and does not replace those separate statutory controls.

official_measurement_examples.name: Amendment separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Changing or ending a covenant and amending a biodiversity gain registration are separate processes; neither can be assumed from a later planning decision.

core_rules: conservation covenant is not planning permission
conservation covenant is a local land charge
covenant existence does not imply public access
responsible body designation must be current
covenant is distinct from BNG gain-site registration
gain-site allocation is distinct from covenant existence
covenant does not prove current title ownership
covenant does not replace statutory designations
covenant duration and obligations must retain agreement-specific terms
LLC search absence in non-migrated or incomplete contexts is not definitive absence
amendment or discharge is not inferred from planning status
covenant evidence does not establish development capacity
no parcel covenant clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Defra, Natural England, HM Land Registry, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. The 14 May 2026 responsible-body list and 2 June 2026 biodiversity-gain registration update were retained with LLC, ownership, access, BNG and planning separation; no parcel promotion.
